text:
Checked your eight acceptance criteria against the current tree now that this epic is claimed. Status, with evidence:

  MET  Print/format/coercion - 26 S3method entries (was zero in my first review); as_neurovol() round-trips
       exactly on a masked volume with spacing preserved and correct NA fill.
  MET  README begins with the fMRI problem - now opens "estimate where experimental effects are
       reproducible, how their multivariate geometry changes across the brain, and which local patterns
       generalize across independent runs". That was my original complaint; it is addressed.
  MET  The two package-free contract files are gone, and the independent oracle helpers survive
       (helper-effect-form-laws.R, helper-evidence-pairing-laws.R, helper-measurement-form-oracle.R,
       plus a new helper-residual-statistics.R). That is the product-oracle resolution I asked for.
  GAP  Runnable Rd examples - see bd-01KZY2DW2XHE207JMFPVEV957W. 5 of 82, and they cover the Epic 5-7
       metric/plan family rather than the first journey. geometry, relation, rdm, rsa, contrast,
       compile_frame, searchlights, lm_relation_fit and as_neurovol all have none.
  GAP  Slower-tier gates - bd-01KZXEFHAWJ97VCRJ84JP85GA8. Nothing sets EFFECTAGRAM_RUN_SCALE_TESTS.
  GAP  R CMD check - bd-01KZY1YJ426SEKJM6Q4THDAR7J. Not run in 10708 lines and 43 new man pages.
  GAP  Certified artifact provenance - bd-01KZXFZ4WRKASSWYMDSECG8FED. Still no commit; 20 untracked R files.
  OPEN Scale regime honesty - bd-01KZXWPKT4XPSB55PB5RBSAZRT. The passing gate certifies performance on a
       fixture where 84% of supports have k > residual df. With 1677 s of headroom this is now cheap to
       re-run at a meaningful configuration.
  OPEN bd-01KZXW5MFZGEXVJ3CMKMGBGFZX - MC variance gate at 1% headroom (replications 64 vs SEs pinned at 120).

Suggested ordering, since two of these interact: add the Rd examples FIRST, then run R CMD check once. Examples are executed by the check, so doing it the other way means certifying a check and then enlarging its surface.
